fences.rule: If the case is read as the setting that must be built so strangers can compare private memories, it is here as Room for strangers; read as the preemption that kept that setting from ever forming, it is there as Unassembled witness, the same tenant-class mechanism seen from the other seat.
fences.case: Eight tenants each know one eviction and none knows a landlord, and the comparison has nowhere to happen.

fences.rule: Every member here answers Unborn witness, the question 'What must first be built so their difference can leave a trace?', so the map presupposes that metamorphosis and holds the instruments and settings the answer must bring into existence, while the transformed question itself stays there.
fences.case: Two accounts of one event disagree and the present world cannot produce evidence that separates them, so the question turns from which account is right to what must first be built.
